newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima denies applying for court protection.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima denies applying for court protection.

text.p: Tobishima Corp on Friday denied market talk that it has applied for court protection from its creditors.
The denial came in a statement issued by the construction company after a sharp fall in its share price.

As of 0405 GMT, the share price was down 50 yen at 151 yen, ranked as the second-steepest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It briefly dipped to 500 yen. Volume was 3.629 million shares, the seventh heaviest trading on the first section.
"The rumour about us applying at the court for protection from creditors is not true at all," Tobishima's president Shoichiro Ishihara said in a statement.
In October 1996, the company announced a restructuring plan with the aim of bouncing back from its financial difficulties.
Under the plan, it asked creditors to reduce their claims against Tobishima for the debts owed by its group companies from about 740 billion yen to 100 billion yen.
The plan also provides that Tobishima would pay back the guaranteed loans over the next 20 years upon request of the creditors.
"There are some financial institutions that need more time before giving their final consent, but we are confident that all of them will eventually agree to our restructuring plan," Ishihara said.
